title: Alert noise review + tuning for Private observability minimum pack
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
We have the initial PrometheusRule bundle for the **Private observability minimum pack** (SLO burn alerts, availability/latency/error alerts, resource exhaustion, and pipeline health). Before GA / bundling into the Private installer release train, we need to **run rules against staging load**, measure expected fire rates, and tune to avoid paging noise.

This ticket owns:
- Running the full rule set in staging under representative load (including failure injection where feasible)
- Adjusting thresholds/window pairs where noisy
- Adding suppression/inhibition where appropriate (e.g., suppress symptom alerts during known upstream outages)
- Defining paging policy (what pages vs tickets, defaults for sev mapping)

## Goals
- Operators get a usable baseline without getting paged for normal bursty traffic or transient collector hiccups
- Pages correspond to actionable outages (availability/SLO burn, hard resource exhaustion)
- Non-actionable or “FYI” conditions go to ticket/Slack by default

## Non-goals
- Customer-specific tuning for unique traffic patterns (document how to tune; do not ship bespoke defaults)
- Building a new alerting backend (stick to Prometheus rules + Alertmanager routing assumptions)

## Inputs / references
- Drive: **private-min-pack-alert-noise-review-sheet** (tracking observed fire rates and decisions)
- GitHub: observability-pack PRs **#322** (SLO + critical availability), **#323** (pipeline health + missing signals)
- Slack: eng-sre thread on severity mapping + paging policy

## Work plan
1) **Deploy** rule bundle to staging ("private-staging-usw2") with representative dashboards enabled.
2) **Generate load**:
   - baseline: 2–3h normal load replay
   - burst: 10m bursts (2–3x baseline) to test rate-limits/queueing behavior
   - failure injection: simulated scrape failure for one target; simulated log forwarder backpressure
3) **Collect data**:
   - per-rule fire count, duration, and annotations
   - top sources of flapping and false positives
   - correlation with known incidents/events during the window
4) **Tune**:
   - adjust thresholds (latency/error windows and burn-rate window pairs)
   - add `for:` clauses where appropriate
   - refine label filters (avoid alerting on low-traffic routes)
   - add inhibition guidance / default alert grouping guidance
5) **Define paging policy** (default):
   - Sev1 pages: availability SLO burn (fast burn), gateway 5xx critical, control plane down, GPU OOM / hard saturation impacting serving
   - Sev2 tickets: slow burn, elevated errors without SLO burn, pipeline degradation with buffered backlog but not dropping
   - Sev3/info: missing signals (warn) with clear runbook steps and reasonable delays
6) **Update docs**:
   - add "Default routing" section to alerting philosophy doc
   - add tuning knobs + recommended per-customer overrides in config reference

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Noise review sheet filled for all rule groups (SLO burn, availability, latency, errors, resources, pipeline health, missing signals)
- [x] Updated thresholds/window pairs merged with justification in PR description
- [x] Any new suppression/inhibition recommendations documented (Alertmanager rules guidance)
- [x] Clear paging policy shipped: which alerts are paging by default and why
- [x] Staging run produces **< 1 page/day equivalent** under normal traffic (excluding deliberate failure injection)

## Notes / heuristics agreed w/ SRE
- Prefer **burn-rate** over raw p99 latency thresholds when possible (fewer false positives during short bursts).
- For low-traffic tenants/routes: avoid percentile-based latency alerts unless traffic floor is met.
- Pipeline health alerts must distinguish between “collector down” vs “temporary backpressure” (page only on drops / sustained export failures).
comments:
2025-02-18 — Talia Benson (creator)
Created as release-blocker for Private min pack. Please keep the Drive noise sheet updated as decisions are made so Docs can capture rationale.

Requested reviewers: Sean (paging), Allison (standards), Sergio (rules author).

2025-02-20 — Sergio Costa
Deployed current rule bundle to private-staging-usw2 under folder `private-min-pack`. Observed early flapping on `GatewayHigh5xxRate` during canary rollout (not customer-like). Suggest we add a `for: 10m` and/or suppress when `deploy_in_progress` annotation present (we already emit deploy annotations in staging).

Also: `MissingMetricsExporter` warning fired immediately due to one sandbox namespace not scraping. We should scope missing-signal alerts to namespaces with `redwood_private_install="true"` label (installer can set).

Linking: observability-pack PR #323 has the missing-signals group; will patch there once SRE agrees.

2025-02-21 — Sean Gallagher
Agree on scoping missing-signals to installed components only. For paging policy: we should not page for "missing signals" by default—ticket only, unless it blocks SLO evaluation (e.g., no gateway request metric at all).

For 5xx: don’t rely on deploy annotations in Private installs (customers won’t have our deploy tooling). Prefer `for:` + require minimum request volume to avoid paging on tiny denominators. Add a traffic floor like `rate(requests_total[5m]) > 1` or similar per-tenant aggregation.

Action item: update `GatewayHigh5xxRate` and `GatewayAvailabilitySLOBurn` to include request floor and reduce flapping.

2025-02-25 — Allison Grant
Reviewed current rules for cardinality + label usage. One concern: some alerts group by `model` which will explode for customers with many versions pinned. Recommend grouping by `model_family` (or drop model label) for paging alerts; keep model breakdown in dashboards only.

Also, if we’re adding request floors, document them in the minimum signals standard as "alerting expectations" (not a hard metric requirement).

2025-02-27 — Sean Gallagher
Staging replay (3h baseline + 2 bursts) results summary (details in noise sheet):
- SLO burn alerts: OK (no unexpected fires). Fast burn triggered only during deliberate 10m 5xx injection.
- Latency p99 alert: too noisy during burst; moved to ticket-only and raised window to 15m with traffic floor.
- GPU high util: fired constantly at ~85–92% util under normal batching. Changed to page only on sustained throttling/OOM signals and queue growth correlation; util alert becomes informational.
- Pipeline backlog: collector backlog grew during burst but recovered; page only if backlog is growing AND drops > 0 OR export failures sustained 15m.

Requested Sergio to implement rule edits and update annotations (runbook links + severity labels).

2025-03-03 — Sergio Costa
Implemented changes in observability-pack:
- Added request floors to gateway error/latency alerts
- Converted raw GPU util alert to info; added GPU OOM + sustained throttling + queue correlation for paging
- Scoped missing-signals alerts to `redwood_private_install="true"` + added `for: 30m`
- Reduced grouping labels (removed `model` from paging alerts)

PRs:
- observability-pack PR #326 (noise tuning round 1)
- slo-toolkit PR #146 (helper for request floor + burn-rate annotations)

Please review especially the label changes; dashboards still use `model` in panels so debugging is unaffected.

2025-03-06 — Sean Gallagher
Reviewed PR #326. Looks good. One more tweak: make `ControlPlaneDown` alert page only after `for: 5m` to avoid startup noise during upgrades; add separate `ControlPlaneUnreachable` warning with `for: 1m` for faster operator visibility (ticket/Slack).

Also confirming default paging policy for GA:
- Paging (Sev1): Availability fast burn; sustained 5xx with volume; GPU OOM / hard throttling impacting throughput; control plane down; rule-evaluation failing.
- Ticket (Sev2): slow burn; elevated latency; pipeline degradation.
- Info (Sev3): missing signals; nearing resource saturation.

Doc ask: include "customer override" snippet for routing all alerts to ticket-only if they’re not ready to page.

2025-03-10 — Sergio Costa
Applied Sean’s final tweak in PR #326 (added control plane warn vs down split, adjusted `for:`). Re-ran staging with 2h baseline: zero paging candidates fired. Only info alerts were `GPUUtilHigh` and `CollectorBacklogGrowing` during burst windows (expected).

2025-03-14 — Talia Benson
Marking done after merge + doc handoff.

Merged:
- observability-pack PR #326
- slo-toolkit PR #146

Follow-ups filed:
- ENG-2872: Add installer label `redwood_private_install=true` on all pack components so missing-signals scoping is robust
- ENG-2873: Add upgrade-mode inhibit example to operator docs (customer Alertmanager)

Docs team (Elliot/Kira) updated alerting philosophy + config reference with paging policy and tuning knobs.
